_about: Researched positions and altitudes for Taita Taveta. See docs/place-data-sources.md. 'sourced' = from a published source; 'approximate' = an estimate to verify on site.

places.name: Wundanyi
places.blurb: The hill town at the heart of Taita life: terraced slopes, a busy market, and the starting point for the Ngangao forest and Wesu Rock.
places.note: Altitude from a weather service's terrain model (about 1,408 m); a surveyed figure would be better.

places.name: Voi
places.blurb: The county's largest town and gateway to Tsavo East: a railway town, a meat and produce market for the hills, and lodges on its edges.

places.name: Mwatate
places.blurb: The county's administrative seat, once the district headquarters, set between the hills and the sisal estates of the plains.

places.name: Lake Chala
places.blurb: A deep crater lake shared with Tanzania, fed from Kilimanjaro's forests below ground. The rim path gives long views across the plains.
places.note: Crocodiles live in the lake: walk the rim, don't swim.

places.name: Lake Jipe
places.blurb: A shallow lake at the south-western end of Tsavo West, shared with Tanzania, with fishing villages, hippos and a lot of birds.
places.note: No reliable altitude found yet: left empty.

places.name: Mbololo Forest
places.blurb: One of the largest and best-kept cloud forests on the Taita Hills, home to birds found nowhere else on Earth.
places.note: The forest spans 1,400–1,700 m; 1,550 m is the middle of that range.

places.name: Ngangao Forest
places.blurb: A misty indigenous cloud forest about 10 km from Wundanyi, easy to reach and walk, with a basic forest camp beside it.
places.note: 2,149 m is the peak above the forest. The position is estimated from 'about 10 km from Wundanyi'; please verify on site.

places.name: Taita Hills Wildlife Sanctuary
places.blurb: A privately run sanctuary of about 110 square kilometres beside Tsavo West, with elephants, big cats and the endemic Taita birds.
places.note: 1,200 m is the sanctuary's own figure. The position is an estimate; please verify on site.

places.name: Mount Kasigau
places.blurb: An isolated, steep-sided mountain rising from the plains to a cloud-forest summit, with a hiking route and community-guided camps.
places.note: Rises from about 550 m; cloud forest above about 1,250 m.

places.name: Vuria Peak
places.blurb: The highest point in the Taita Hills and in the county, reached on a stiff walk through forest and farmland.
places.note: Sources disagree: 2,208 m (local constituency, University of Helsinki station), 2,228 m (Wikipedia, BirdLife, Kenya Tourism Board), 2,257 m (a field-course GPS reading). The position is estimated from the range's centre.

places.name: Sagalla Hill
places.blurb: A steep hill directly south of Voi, rewarding early starts with a sunrise over Tsavo's red earth and, on a clear day, a glimpse of Kilimanjaro.
places.note: 1,450 m is the peak height. The position is estimated from 'directly south of Voi'; please verify on site.

places.name: Teita Sisal Estate
places.blurb: One of the largest sisal estates in the world, near Mwatate: rows of spiky green on the plains, and the families whose lives follow the harvest.
places.note: Described as 'near Mwatate'; the position and altitude are estimates.

places.name: Dawida Kitchens
places.blurb: Home cooks around Wundanyi opening their kitchens for the dishes of the hills.
places.note: A sample listing placed in Wundanyi's centre.

places.name: Wundanyi Grounds
places.blurb: The town's football ground, where the hills turn up on a Saturday.
places.note: A sample listing placed near Wundanyi's centre.
